claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm responsible for - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are some specific rules that apply. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he attending school, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! He's currently studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is 17 and in approved education (studying A-levels at sixth form), that's positive for your eligibility.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now let me ask:

**Are you the person who is responsible for Alex - meaning either you live with him, or you're paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards his upkeep (like food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me, so I'm responsible for all his day-to-day needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one final question:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, started an apprenticeship, or started receiving benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't. He's just focused on his A-levels at the moment - no job, no apprenticeship, and he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- Alex is 17 years old and studying A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education
- You can claim Child Benefit for children aged 16-19 as long as they stay in approved education or training
- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you, so you're responsible for him
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex hasn't started paid work of 24+ hours per week, an apprenticeship, or started receiving benefits in his own right

**Important things to note:**

- Child Benefit can continue until Alex finishes his A-levels or turns 20, whichever comes first
- If his circumstances change (for example, if he leaves education, starts working 24+ hours per week, or starts an apprenticeship), you'll need to inform HMRC
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

You can apply for Child Benefit if you haven't already done so. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
